candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — mechanism and meal-related administration of a phosphate binder
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that sevelamer carbonate lowers serum phosphorus by binding dietary phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract and reducing intestinal absorption.

options.A: Sevelamer remains in the gastrointestinal tract and binds dietary phosphate, decreasing intestinal phosphate absorption and lowering serum phosphorus.
options.B: Sevelamer lowers phosphorus primarily by increasing renal phosphate filtration and urinary excretion.
options.C: Sevelamer increases intestinal phosphate absorption so the kidneys can remove phosphorus more efficiently.
options.D: Sevelamer has no direct effect on phosphate absorption and is used mainly as a systemic diuretic.

candidate.rationale: Current FDA labeling describes sevelamer carbonate as a nonabsorbed phosphate-binding polymer. In the intestine, its protonated amine groups interact with phosphate; by binding phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract and decreasing absorption, sevelamer lowers serum phosphorus. Its effect therefore depends on contact with dietary phosphate in the gut rather than renal filtration or systemic diuresis. A is correct; B, C, and D misstate the labeled mechanism.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports the drug-specific mechanism of sevelamer carbonate as gastrointestinal phosphate binding with reduced intestinal absorption rather than renal excretion.
candidate.source_document_title: SEVELAMER CARBONATE tablets — Official Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Full Prescribing Information → Section 12.1, Mechanism of Action: sevelamer carbonate is a nonabsorbed phosphate-binding cross-linked polymer; protonated amines in the intestine interact with phosphate through ionic and hydrogen bonding; binding phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract decreases absorption and lowers serum phosphorus. Current Renvela labeling also states that sevelamer carbonate taken with meals controls serum phosphorus in CKD patients on dialysis.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease on dialysis is prescribed sevelamer carbonate with meals for elevated serum phosphorus. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?
